title: Enklitike
theme: Ja se zovem works because se sits in second place, and Se zovem fails.
reviewerNotes: Pedagogy re-audit after Fact Checker. Second-place clitics only. Merged theme, swapped Sebilj civic photos for café/kahva/toast, tightened englishLies, fixed nerd scholar voice, softened trick lock wording, trimmed look[6] matching gloss, shortened se/sam cards, fixed q6 distractor. Kept Vidim ga and Ja sam pila pivo Bosnian. Still draft. Final native try/quiz sweep: removed cat-plot/joke weak distractors; replaced select meta slots with named undrilled drills (Ano, za njega, Hoću, Pijte, Doći ću, tata, Nema auta, moja prijateljica); Ch11 trebati personal+acc left untouched; status draft.

whyHere.heading: Why you are here
whyHere.body: Today you learn why Ja se zovem Ana works and Se zovem Ana does not. Little words like se, mi, sam, and ću need a seat in second place in the sentence. English lets myself and me wander. Bosnian parks these short words right after the first stressed chunk. Book 1 already gave you Zovem se Ana. This chapter is only that parking rule.

englishLies.heading: Why English lies
englishLies.body: English lies because short words can sit almost anywhere. You can say I call myself Ana, or My name is Ana, and nobody checks the second slot. Bosnian still uses short words for the same jobs, and those short words refuse to open the sentence. Se in zovem se, mi in Drago mi je, sam in a past line, and ću in a future line all ride in second place. Schools call the short pack enklitike, which means clitics. You can keep saying little words in second place and still be right.

knownLine.heading: A line you already say
knownLine.body: Book 1 already gave you Ana’s meeting line Zovem se Ana, which means my name is Ana. The same rule lets her say Ja se zovem Ana. In both lines se sits in second place. Zovem holds first place in the short version. Ja holds first place when she puts herself up front. Se zovem Ana fails because se tried to open the sentence, and Bosnian will not let that little word start.
knownLine.speaker: Ana

pattern.heading: The pattern
pattern.body: Put one stressed word or short phrase first, then park the little word. Ja se zovem Ana puts Ja first and se second. Zovem se Ana puts Zovem first and se second. Drago mi je puts Drago first and mi second. Pio sam pivo puts Pio first and sam second. Ja ću doći puts Ja first and ću second. You may shuffle the big words for stress or style. You may not shove se, mi, sam, or ću into first place. Second place is the whole job for this chapter.

howYouGuess.heading: The pests
howYouGuess.body: Three pests will trip you today, and all three come from English word order. The first pest is starting with se, as in Se zovem Ana. The second pest is parking the little word at the English end, as in Ja zovem se Ana. The third pest is opening with sam or ću alone, as in Sam pio pivo or Ću doći. Fix them the same way. Put a real first word down, then seat the little word. Zovem se, Pio sam, and Ja ću all clear the rule.

trick.heading: The bit that tricks you
trick.body: The trap is to think Ja must always sit in the sentence for the rule to work. That is not true. Zovem se Ana already has a first place word, so se is happy in second place with no Ja at all. The other trap is to treat every short Bosnian word like a free English pronoun. After a preposition you need the long form from Chapter 7, so za mene stays long while me alone is the short rider for other seats. Today you only park the little word in second place. The long-versus-short chart already had its day.

nerd.heading: Why it's like this
nerd.body:
Bosnian parks short words like se, mi, sam, and ću in second place in the sentence. Schools sometimes call that Wackernagel's law, which just means little words sit in second place. Se in Ja se zovem follows that seat rule. English lets myself and me wander more freely, so the parking habit is easier to miss if you start from English.

The meaning is not in a free English slot. The seat is the rule.

items.prompt: Pick the line that parks se correctly.
items.explanation: Ja is first. Se is second. The other two break the parking rule.

items.prompt: Book 1 also uses Zovem se Emir. Where does se sit?
items.explanation: Zovem is first. Se is second. Ja is not required.

items.prompt: Someone says Se zovem Ana. What went wrong?
options: They needed a leftover pile ending
Se tried to open the sentence
Ana switched to the he pile
items.explanation: Little words cannot take first place. Put Ja or Zovem first.

items.prompt: Drago mi je. What sits in second place?
options: Only je, with mi free at the end
items.explanation: Drago is first. Mi and je ride together in second place. Je is a little word too.

items.prompt: Past line. Which form parks sam correctly?
items.explanation: Pio is first. Sam is second. Sam cannot open the line.

items.prompt: Future line. Which form parks ću correctly?
items.explanation: Ja is first. Ću is second. Ću alone cannot lead.

items.prompt: Does Zovem se Ana need Ja to be legal?
options: No. Zovem already fills first place.
Yes. Se is illegal unless Ja is written.
items.explanation: First place can be Ja or a stressed doing-word like Zovem.

items.prompt: Daj mi kahvu. Why is mi second?
options: Because mi is a little word that parks after Daj
Because want-it jobs always start with mi
items.explanation: Daj is first. Mi is second. Kahvu still shows the want-it job on coffee.

items.prompt: Ja zovem se Ana. What failed?
options: Se arrived too late for second place
items.explanation: After Ja, the next seat belongs to se. Zovem se without Ja is fine. Ja zovem se is not.

items.prompt: Pick the future line that parks ću with the infinitive first.
items.explanation: Doći can take first place, so ću still sits second. Ću alone cannot lead.

questions.question: Why does Se zovem Ana fail?
options: Because se cannot take first place
questions.explanation: Little words sit in second place. Ja se zovem and Zovem se both work.

questions.question: In Zovem se Emir, what holds first place?
options: A silent Ja that must be written
questions.explanation: Zovem is the stressed first chunk. Se parks right after it.

questions.question: In Drago mi je, where do mi and je sit?
questions.explanation: Drago is first. The little words mi and je share second place.

questions.question: Which past line parks sam correctly?
questions.explanation: Pio is first. Sam is second. Sam cannot open the sentence.

questions.question: Which future line parks ću correctly?
questions.explanation: Ja is first. Ću is second. Doći ću also works because Doći can take first place.

questions.question: What comes next after little words in second place?
options: A full pronoun and tense re-teach
A mixed review of the whole notebook
questions.explanation: Chapter 13 reviews piles, jobs, matching, doing-words, and this parking rule.

next.body: You now know why Ja se zovem and Zovem se both work, and why Se zovem fails. Little words like se, mi, sam, and ću sit in second place. Chapter 13 is the mixed review of the whole notebook, from piles to this parking rule. There is no new system tomorrow.
